purpose: Isolate fixed receive-slot scans and redundant gauge summation from the November 6 performance review.
method: Two production/candidate/production comparisons. Thirty seconds per point, persistent daemons within each phase, disjoint CPU placement. No local builds, kernel tests or Git packing overlap load. CPU uses before/sent process and thread ticks; 100% is one core. Goodput uses receiver sample bytes/time; missing uses final receiver counts after drain. Counter deltas include drain.
candidate: One u64 occupied receive-slot mask per session; flush_taps/deadline visit set bits, connection barriers test mask emptiness, and reassembly gauges accumulate during the existing flush. Receive budgets, frame deadlines, admission and ACK rules are unchanged.
disposition: Rejected: reverse 4G goodput is below both controls in both comparisons; high-load CPU reductions do not establish a consistent bidirectional gain.
counter_units: Queue drops count source buffers or control records; a dropped GSO source can contain many frames. TAP and socket drops count SKBs, expiry counts frame classes. Do not sum them as exact frame losses.

checks: sparse slots 0/63, retained gauges, ACK and expiry deadlines
failed lane return to an earlier free slot, eventual connection barrier completion
